title: "http://trusted.com@evil.com/" goes to evil.com, not trusted.com - and both languages' real parsers already know that
assumption: A URL string that starts with (or contains) "trusted.com" points at trusted.com.

input.description: A link in a phishing email, a redirect parameter, or a webhook target URL that a naive check validates by looking for a trusted domain name somewhere in the string - `url.startsWith("http://trusted.com")` or a regex containing `trusted\.com`.

what_goes_wrong: A substring/prefix check for "trusted.com" passes on `http://trusted.com@evil.com/`, but the browser (or any real HTTP client) actually connects to `evil.com` - `trusted.com` here is just userinfo (a username with no password), not the host, and both a proper WHATWG `URL` parse and Python's `urlparse` agree the real host is `evil.com`.
why: RFC 3986's authority component has the shape `userinfo@host:port` - everything before an `@` in the authority is credentials, not part of the hostname, and both a real URL parser and the browser's address bar logic strip it before deciding where to connect. A regex or `startsWith` check that only looks for the trusted domain's text anywhere near the front of the string has no concept of URL grammar at all, so it is fooled by a syntax feature (`@`) that every conformant parser already understands correctly. This is not a parser disagreement - it's a gap between "looks like it mentions the right domain" and "actually parses to the right host".

repros.code:
from urllib.parse import urlparse
u = urlparse("http://trusted.com@evil.com/")
print(u.hostname, u.username)
print("http://trusted.com@evil.com/".startswith("http://trusted.com"))

fix: Never validate a URL's target by substring or prefix matching on the raw string. Parse the URL and compare the parsed `.hostname` against an allowlist of exact hostnames (or a proper suffix match on the hostname component specifically, e.g. ends with `.trusted.com`), never against the whole URL text.

sources.title: RFC 3986: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax, Section 3.2

test_cases.note: their_is_trusted_url(url) must parse the URL and check the hostname field - not check whether the string contains or starts with the trusted domain's text - or this input will pass a check it should fail.
